title: Scientists Create Bananas That Stay Yellow Longer
paragraphs: You're in the mood for a fresh snack at the supermarket, and you decide on a fruit salad. But when you see the banana pieces looking brown and soft mixed in with the fresh-looking apple slices, grapes and pineapple chunks, you decide to get something else instead.
Those banana pieces may still be fine to eat, but the way they look can put people off — and it can mean they get thrown away.
But now, scientists may have found a way to help.
British company Tropic has created a gene-edited banana that stays yellow for longer after it is peeled or cut.

Tropic says the new bananas look and taste normal, but the inside can stay yellow for an extra day or two — and even longer when kept cold. This makes them especially useful in prepackaged foods such as fruit salads and breakfast bowls.
The company also says the non-browning bananas could cut food waste and emissions.
Banana waste is a big problem. One UK government study found that about 1.4 million bananas that are still good to eat are thrown away in Britain every day.

The gene-edited bananas have moved closer to being sold in the UK, after the government confirmed they are "precision-bred." This means their genes were edited in a way that could also have happened if they were bred in a traditional way.
But they must still be approved by the UK's Food Standards Agency before they can be sold in supermarkets.
The non-browning bananas have already been approved for sale in 10 other countries, including Japan, Brazil and the Philippines.
